findings.suppression_reason: Pipeline service role needs account-wide access across the services it orchestrates; matches the existing checkov skips. Consumers can supply their own role via role_arn.
findings.title: Pipeline role can PassRole any role to CloudFormation/EC2/ECS/Beanstalk while holding ec2:*, ecs:*, elasticbeanstalk:* on *
findings.explanation: iam:PassRole is granted on Resource "*" (limited only by iam:PassedToService with StringEqualsIfExists), and the same document grants ec2:*, ecs:*, elasticbeanstalk:* and rds:* on "*". Anyone who can edit the pipeline can launch an EC2/ECS task or CloudFormation stack with any role in the account, including an administrator role, which is a privilege escalation path. HLD_AWS_222 flags the wildcard resource but not the PassRole + compute-launch composition, and StringEqualsIfExists passes whenever the key is absent.
findings.remediation: Scope iam:PassRole to the specific role ARNs the pipeline's deploy targets use (a variable such as pass_role_arns), switch the condition to StringEquals, and replace the service-wide wildcard actions with the specific actions the stages need.

findings.title: Example KMS key policy is a bare statement without Version/Statement wrapper, so apply fails
findings.explanation: The heredoc policy is a single statement object ({Sid, Effect, Principal, Action, Resource}) with no Version and no Statement array. KMS rejects this with MalformedPolicyDocumentException, so the example cannot be applied, and holden's HLD_AWS_292/HLD_AWS_317 checks stayed Unknown because the document does not parse as a policy. Read as intended, the statement only delegates to the account root, so no wildcard principal or logs-service grant exists (both unresolved checks are safe). The example is the module's documented usage, so a broken key blocks every consumer who copies it.
findings.remediation: Wrap the statement in a policy document, ideally with jsonencode, and add deletion_window_in_days.

findings.title: Module requires a CMK for the artifact store but the role it creates has no KMS permissions
findings.explanation: aws_codepipeline.pipe always sets artifact_store.encryption_key to var.kms_key_arn (required, no default), yet the generated policy has no kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey* or kms:DescribeKey grant. With the usual key policy that delegates to IAM (as in the example), the module-created role cannot read or write artifacts and the pipeline fails at the first stage. It only works when the caller grants the role KMS access separately or supplies role_arn.
findings.remediation: Add a statement granting kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey*, kms:DescribeKey on var.kms_key_arn to the policy document, or document that callers must grant it.

findings.title: Artifact bucket has no bucket policy denying non-TLS requests
findings.explanation: The example defines no aws_s3_bucket_policy, so requests over plain HTTP are accepted. The bucket holds source and build artifacts, and no built-in policy covers TLS enforcement for aws_s3_bucket (coverage lists only encryption, public access block, logging, versioning, lifecycle and object lock).
findings.remediation: Add an aws_s3_bucket_policy with a Deny on s3:* when aws:SecureTransport is false.

findings.title: Module uses data.aws_region.current.name, deprecated in AWS provider 6.x
findings.explanation: The example pins hashicorp/aws 6.43.0, where the region data source's name attribute is deprecated in favour of region. It is used in locals.tf, aws_pipeline.pipe.tf (action region default) and the example's locals.tf, so consumers get deprecation warnings. The module declares no provider constraint, so switching to .region would break consumers still on provider 5.x; the right fix depends on the supported range, which is why it is not marked fixable.
findings.remediation: Move to data.aws_region.current.region and add a required_providers constraint of aws >= 6 to the module, or keep .name and document the 5.x support range.

suggested_policies.rationale: S3 buckets should enforce TLS with a bucket policy denying aws:SecureTransport = false. No built-in policy covers this for aws_s3_bucket; the check needs to inspect the content of the companion policy, which the DSL's requires_companion cannot do.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_AWS_001
name: S3 buckets must have a bucket policy that denies non-TLS requests
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  Without a Deny on aws:SecureTransport = false, clients can read and write
  objects over plain HTTP, exposing data and credentials-bearing requests to
  interception.
message: |
  aws_s3_bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false.
remediation: |
  Add an aws_s3_bucket_policy with a Deny statement on s3:* for the bucket and
  its objects, conditioned on Bool aws:SecureTransport = false.
resources:
  aws_s3_bucket:
    requires_companion:
      type: aws_s3_bucket_policy
      via: bucket
      where:
        path: policy
        contains: aws:SecureTransport
suggested_policies.dsl_extension_note: requires_companion.where needs a substring/JSON-aware match on the companion's policy attribute (statement with Effect Deny and Condition Bool aws:SecureTransport = false). A plain string 'contains' on the rendered policy JSON is enough to implement the minimal version.
